why: January is when the Majlis hosts the Hero Dubai Desert Classic (21-24 Jan 2027), billed as played 'under the Dubai winter sun'; the Majlis was the Middle East's first grass course (1988).
tradeoff: Desert Classic week pulls 'thousands of fans' to the Majlis, and the Dubai winter is the emirate's busiest golf window.

why: Southern-hemisphere midsummer: an 18-hole par-72 on Lake Wakatipu beneath The Remarkables, with 5 Jan-30 Apr priced as the season and long warm days.
tradeoff: Summer is peak season in Queenstown (20-30C) and visitor green fees peak too; the course shuts for mid-winter maintenance (22 Jun-14 Aug).

why: Marrakech's golf high season runs 5 September-30 June, so January is prime; Kyle Phillips routed 18 holes blending Moroccan oases with 'an astonishing Scottish touch'.
tradeoff: High-season green fees apply for visitors, and Marrakech's inland winter is 'less Mediterranean and more continental'.

why: Portugal offers 'pleasant temperatures even in winter', and Oitavos Dunes (3rd in Lisbon, top-100 continental Europe) mixes woodland and links-type holes.
tradeoff: Lisbon's winter means 'colder and shorter days' - good for prices, tighter for 18 holes - on an Atlantic-exposed site.

why: The PGA Tour's Farmers Insurance Open is staged at Torrey Pines 'each year, in January or February', making January prime clifftop golf weather in San Diego.
tradeoff: The tournament takes over both courses (final rounds on the South), disrupting public play around event week.

why: Antalya enjoys 'three hundred days of sunshine' and a 'mild winter'; the Montgomerie course is built on pure sand among Mediterranean pines in Belek.
tradeoff: Mediterranean winter rounds run into early dusk, which is why the club floodlights its back nine.

why: The Stadium Course hosts the WM Phoenix Open, 'the PGA TOUR stop with the largest crowds of any golf event in the world', and Scottsdale's desert season peaks in February.
tradeoff: February is the peak and priciest month, and tournament week packs the course and the 16th's 'Coliseum' with record crowds.

why: February brings mild daytime golf before Marrakech's fierce summer heat; Royal Golf Marrakech's Old course is the Golias–Massy parkland layout distinguished by the Moroccan golf federation.
tradeoff: Marrakech winter mornings and nights stay cool, and rain is possible; confirm an Old-course tee time rather than assuming the Menara layout.

why: February is late antipodean summer (18.6-25.8C); NSW Golf Club occupies 'one of the most spectacular coastal settings in world golf' on the La Perouse cliffs.
tradeoff: Sydney's summer humidity spikes to 65%, so clifftop rounds can turn muggy.

why: Late-summer Queenstown gives long, warm 20-30C days in a natural alpine amphitheatre, with Millbrook the home of the New Zealand Open.
tradeoff: Summer is peak season, so accommodation and flights are busiest and most expensive.

why: Early February still trades on Thailand's cool season before the heat builds (February is cooler than March and April); Thai CC hosted the 1997 Asian Honda Classic won by Tiger Woods.
tradeoff: February is the changeover from cool to hot season, and December-February is Thailand's most expensive accommodation period.

why: Egypt's 'moderate, cool winter' runs November-February and is called 'the optimal tourist season'; Katameya is a desert-oasis resort course first opened in 1997.
tradeoff: Winter is Egypt's busiest season, with pricier flights and hotels and heavily visited sites.

why: Cape Town Tourism: 'March is the beginning of the shoulder season, when the summer holiday crowds have left', with 15-27C and an average of just two rainy days.
tradeoff: Big event weekends (Two Oceans Marathon, Cape Town Cycle Tour, Easter) fill the city and can push prices up.

why: Autumn (March-May) is 'the mildest time of year in Sydney when the humidity drops' (14.6-22.2C), suiting a MacKenzie clifftop layout.
tradeoff: Temperatures fall to around 14.6C at the cool end, so early tee times as summer fades can be brisk.

why: March still sits in Lisbon's quiet, low-price 'December to March' budget window while the weather warms toward spring.
tradeoff: Spring in Lisbon brings 'occasional rainfall', and the exposed Atlantic links can be windy.

why: 'Autumn sets in from March' in Queenstown, and autumn is one of the 'quieter seasons' when you get 'a better deal on flights and accommodation'.
tradeoff: Autumn temperatures swing from 5C to 25C, so layers matter as summer fades.

why: Egypt's spring (March-April) is 'short and sweet', 'neither extremely hot nor uncomfortably cold', with fewer crowds and lower prices than winter.
tradeoff: Spring carries 'a potential for sandstorms known as the khamsin', and temperatures can be erratic.

why: March closes out Barcelona's mild 15C/6C, 173-sunshine-hour January-March window as spring begins in Spain.
tradeoff: Winter March weather still needs layers and an umbrella, with cold starts to the day.

why: April opens Melbourne's sandbelt autumn, one of the city's two best-weather windows; Top 100 ranks Royal Melbourne West as Australia's best course and one of Alister MacKenzie's finest designs (planned 1926).
tradeoff: Royal Melbourne is a private club: visitor tee times are limited and must be booked well ahead, and autumn is peak sandbelt demand.

why: April brings milder days and more sunshine than March in Edinburgh's Gogarbank normals, a spring benefit for Muirfield's East Lothian links; Harry Colt revised the layout in 1925.
tradeoff: Visitor play at private Muirfield is on Tuesdays and Thursdays with a recognised handicap limit; April can still turn wet and windy.

why: Rome's best window is April to early June: warm, long days, and prices below the summer peak. Marco Simone, the 2023 Ryder Cup parkland course a short drive from the city, is at its most playable then.
tradeoff: The visitor directory lists Tuesday closure and tighter weekend access; book ahead, check the handicap rule and allow for spring showers.

why: April is Queenstown's golden autumn - warm, settled days and low golden light over the hills; Millbrook's alpine links course sits beneath the Remarkables near Arrowtown.
tradeoff: Autumn colour draws crowds and the Arrowtown festival fills accommodation, and the exposed alpine course turns cold as May approaches.

why: Dubai's cooler window runs December to March, so April is the last comfortable month before the heat; the Majlis, the Middle East's first grass course (1988) framed by desert dunes, rewards early tee times.
tradeoff: Dubai's heat climbs steeply after the cool season, so April rounds need early starts, and the Majlis is a busy, premium resort course.

why: Late March to May is Singapore's inter-monsoon period, relatively drier than January; the Serapong, called Singapore's most stunning layout, is a scenic seaside resort round.
tradeoff: Private-club visitor rounds need advance booking and must meet handicap rules; Singapore stays hot and humid, with afternoon thunderstorms possible.

why: Ireland's golf season runs April to October and May/June/September give the best balance of weather, daylight and green fees; Portmarnock, on its own two-mile sandy peninsula, is a classic links at its best.
tradeoff: This private links keeps Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Bank Holidays for members; reserve a designated visitor window and allow for Atlantic rain and wind.

why: May's late-spring warmth suits Wentworth West's Surrey heathland before summer; nearby Wisley's climate normals show milder days than April for golfers with eligible member-guest access.
tradeoff: Wentworth golf is for members and their guests, not open visitor tee-time booking; arrange an eligible introduction before planning a round.

why: May brings lengthening Icelandic daylight for Brautarholt's coastal golf; the club gives a general season from 1 May to 15 October, weather permitting. The current course has 18 holes.
tradeoff: Opening is weather-dependent. Wind can alter plans; late-evening tee times require confirmation rather than assuming daylight guarantees access.

why: May brings milder days than April in Stockholm's long-term climate, a spring-warming benefit for Bro Hof's lakeside Stadium course beside Lake Mälaren.
tradeoff: Spring nights remain cool and the lakeside layout is exposed to wind; the visitor directory requires advance booking and handicap limits, so confirm current access.

why: May's warming days open a more comfortable window on Kennemer's Zandvoort dune links; Schiphol's long-term normals show a clear step up from April, before midsummer.
tradeoff: Private-club visits require caddiemaster approval, club membership and the stated handicap limit; no Sunday greenfee play. North Sea wind and showers remain.

why: May is a Lisbon-region shoulder month still warm with fewer crowds than summer; Praia d'El Rey blends seaside links and parkland holes among Atlantic dunes north of the city.
tradeoff: Praia d'El Rey is an hour north of Lisbon, the Atlantic wind is near-constant, and shoulder-month weather here is unpredictable.

why: June is peak Scottish golf with daylight stretching late into the evening; Muirfield, the Honourable Company of Edinburgh Golfers' Open venue, shows its fast-running links form in championship season.
tradeoff: Muirfield is private with restricted visitor days, and June is qualifying season when the course and local hotels are busiest.

why: June's long Icelandic daylight creates scope for an evening round at Brautarholt. The club offers tee times after 8pm from 1 June to 16 July by special email request.
tradeoff: Evening access requires a special request, not just long daylight. Confirm weather, finishing arrangements and the separate last tee time for carts.

why: June brings further early-summer warmth in Stockholm's long-term climate, improving daytime comfort over May for Bro Hof's lakeside Stadium course.
tradeoff: June is wetter than May in the Stockholm normals; allow for showers and lakeside wind, and confirm the directory's advance-booking and handicap requirements.

why: June falls in Bali's dry season, but Bali National is reported closed for redevelopment since May 2025. Treat the former Nusa Dua layout as historical golf research, not a currently playable recommendation.
tradeoff: A proposed February 2027 reopening is unconfirmed. Obtain written operator confirmation before planning golf; dry-season climate does not establish access.

why: June gives Ireland close to seventeen hours of daylight and sits in the best-golf window (May, June, September); Portmarnock's sandy-peninsula links is in prime summer condition.
tradeoff: Portmarnock is private and walking-only for visitors, with no visitor buggies; June rounds must fit the published visitor windows.

why: June's early-summer warmth and sunshine suit Walton Heath Old's open Surrey heathland; nearby Wisley's long-term normals put daytime conditions well above spring and winter.
tradeoff: This private club publishes weekday morning and weekend midday visitor windows; reserve ahead, check events and keep waterproofs for June showers.

why: Reykjavík's long July daylight makes a late links round possible; Keilir's back nine sits on a lava-fringed peninsula near town, with views to Snæfellsjökull.
tradeoff: July is still cool, with rain and Atlantic wind; pack layers and waterproofs rather than expecting warm-weather golf.

why: Kytäjä's South East course (Thomas McBroom, 2003) plays through forest and along Lake Kytäjä; July is Helsinki's warmest month with 17h59m of daylight for a late tee time.
tradeoff: Helsinki's regional July figures include rain on about 12 days (63mm) and cool nights; pack layers and waterproofs for inland Kytäjä.

why: July is in Bali's dry season; historical accounts describe coastal views and three landscapes at Bali National. The former layout is reported closed for redevelopment, not confirmed available to play.
tradeoff: The proposed February 2027 reopening has not been verified. Check the operating name, updated routing and accepted tee time directly before arranging travel.

why: July is Dublin's warmest month, with long daylight for Portmarnock's duneland links; the club's published 2027 April–September visitor season includes this midsummer window.
tradeoff: Portmarnock is private: visitor days exclude Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Bank Holidays; July showers remain possible. Book designated windows ahead.

why: Bro Hof's Stadium Course (Robert Trent Jones Jnr, 2007) runs as a 'lakeside path' around Lake Mälaren; Stockholm's July days last 17h44m, stretching evening rounds.
tradeoff: July is Stockholm's wettest month (rain on about 9 days, 65mm), and the Stadium Course's water and gusts make it a stern test.

why: Muirfield's links layout was revised by Harry Colt in 1925; July brings Edinburgh's highest temperatures (17.2°C) and long northern evenings.
tradeoff: Private Muirfield takes fourball bookings in July; smaller groups join a cancellation list. Visitor days are Tuesday/Thursday, and rain remains common.

why: Capilano (Stanley Thompson), carved from rainforest against the North Shore Mountains, is a West Coast classic; August keeps Vancouver's settled summer with up to 15h of daylight.
tradeoff: A private club with limited guest access; evenings cool quickly, with August lows near 13°C.

why: Chambers Bay is a true links on Puget Sound and hosted the 2015 U.S. Open, the first in the Pacific Northwest; August is Seattle's warmest, driest month (high 24.6°C).
tradeoff: The exposed links takes wind off the Sound, and Seattle's dry window is short — rain returns in autumn.

why: Fontana, minutes from Vienna, staged the European Tour in Austria 2006–2009 and will host the 2029 World Amateur Team Championship; August is warm at 26.6°C.
tradeoff: Austrian August can be hot and thundery — rain falls on about 8–9 days — and the championship course demands accuracy.

why: New South Wales GC (opened 1928; routed by Dr Alister MacKenzie) sits on the cliffs at La Perouse with ocean vistas; August, though winter, stays mild (high 17.8°C).
tradeoff: It is Sydney's winter: cool, breezy clifftop golf, and the private club allows only limited visitor access.

why: Cog Hill's Dubsdread (Wilson & Lee, 1964, nationally ranked since opening) is a classic Chicago championship parkland; August is the city's warmest month (high 25.3°C).
tradeoff: Chicago's August is humid (about 76%) with rain on some 17 days; allow flexibility for wet weather rather than expecting a dry round.

why: Glen Abbey (Jack Nicklaus) has hosted the RBC Canadian Open 30 times, more than any other venue; August is a warm 24.5°C with long Ontario days.
tradeoff: It is a busy public championship course; August humidity runs about 74% and weekend tee times fill fast.

why: Bethpage Black, a U.S. Open host (2002), is open for green fees 15 April–15 November; September's cooler weather (highs near 24°C) is prime for this famed public course.
tradeoff: The Black is closed Mondays (except holidays) and demand is high, so a tee time needs early booking or the walk-up queue.

why: September is European Masters month on Crans-sur-Sierre's Ballesteros course in Crans-Montana; the 2026 edition ran 3–6 September, bringing championship golf to the Swiss Alps.
tradeoff: Tournament week restricts play: check the next edition and access dates. Geneva is a gateway, not the course location; plan an onward stay in Crans-Montana.

why: The Montgomerie Maxx Royal (Colin Montgomerie with European Golf Design) is an 18-hole championship course on the Belek coast; September still gives long, warm days.
tradeoff: Late-summer heat lingers into September, and the floodlit back nine exists for evening and night rounds.

why: September eases Barcelona's late-summer heat, a more comfortable window for El Prat's Greg Norman-designed holes outside the city; the benefit is cooling, not a dry-season promise.
tradeoff: Autumn rainfall rises from August in the Barcelona normals; allow flexibility for showers and confirm the El Prat layout and visitor tee time.

why: September starts Melbourne's spring warming after winter, before the hotter summer; Royal Melbourne West brings MacKenzie's rolling sandbelt routing to that improving daytime window.
tradeoff: Spring remains cool and showery, not reliably dry; Royal Melbourne is private and visitor enquiries are limited to golfers meeting its access rules.

why: Marco Simone (Jim Fazio; redesigned for the 2023 Ryder Cup) lies in the grounds of an 11th-century castle outside Rome; September eases the Roman heat (average low 15.2°C).
tradeoff: Afternoons remain warm and the open parkland offers little shade — book morning tee times.

why: October stays mild as Lisbon's summer heat eases, suiting Oitavos Dunes' woodland-and-links mix near Cascais; the Atlantic setting remains exposed to wind.
tradeoff: October rainfall rises sharply from summer in the cited Lisbon normals; pack waterproofs and allow flexibility for Atlantic weather.

why: October's spring warmth brings milder daytime golf than Melbourne's winter, before the summer heat; Royal Melbourne West follows MacKenzie's rolling sandbelt routing.
tradeoff: Spring is famously fickle: about 59 mm of rain and changeable winds, so keep tee times flexible.

why: October reopens Dubai's golf season as the ferocious summer eases, on the Middle East's first grass championship course.
tradeoff: Still hot, with October mean daily highs near 35C in the cited normals; choose an early tee time rather than assuming night golf on the Majlis.

why: October cools from Marrakech's September heat while retaining warm days; the federation identifies Royal Golf Marrakech Old as the Golias–Massy layout, distinct from Menara.
tradeoff: Rain begins to increase after summer and nights cool down; request the Old layout explicitly when confirming a visitor tee time.

why: October's inter-monsoon changeover has less rainfall than November and December in Singapore's Changi normals, offering a relative window for the Serapong's harbour-side golf.
tradeoff: Hot, humid and thunderstorm-prone, especially later in the day; Sentosa is private, so arrange visitor access in advance.

why: October's crisp spring air frames alpine golf beneath The Remarkables on Lake Wakatipu, with clear mountain light.
tradeoff: Cool (~15C) and changeable with ~66 mm of rain; weather can close in quickly.

why: November brings Cape Town's warm, relatively dry late spring before the holiday peak; Steenberg pairs that improving golf weather with its Constantia Valley setting beneath Table Mountain.
tradeoff: The city's high season builds toward December, so secure tee times and stays early.

why: November brings Dubai's warm, very dry golf window after the harsher summer heat; the Majlis pairs that improving weather with its established desert championship layout.
tradeoff: Peak season means higher green fees and tighter tee times; book well ahead.

why: November brings a modest temperature dip from October at Singapore's Changi station, easing the heat slightly for Serapong rounds; this is a cooler, not drier, month.
tradeoff: Rainfall rises sharply toward the year-end wet peak, so thunderstorm delays are likely; confirm private-club visitor access before travelling.

why: November's warmer spring days suit Royal Melbourne West before the hotter summer; the benefit is milder daytime weather for MacKenzie's sandbelt golf, not guaranteed firm turf.
tradeoff: Around 63 mm of rain and gusty fronts; keep tee times flexible.

why: Late spring lifts Queenstown to ~18C with long days beneath The Remarkables.
tradeoff: Peak-rate season starts in November and alpine weather stays changeable.

why: November enters Dutch golf's quieter off-season; regional golf guidance notes that free-draining coastal sand extends play on dune links such as Kennemer beyond the summer peak.
tradeoff: Cold, rain and wind shorten the useful day; Kennemer remains private, with caddiemaster approval, handicap rules and no Sunday greenfee play.

why: December brings summer warmth for La Perouse's clifftop golf above Botany Bay; Sydney's long-term normals are warmer than November.
tradeoff: Summer warmth does not mean dry golf: Sydney's December normals still include rain, so keep plans flexible.

why: December's long, warm days (~25C) and minimal rain (~17 mm) put Cape Town golf at its summer peak.
tradeoff: It is peak holiday season; the course, the city and tee sheets are at their busiest.

why: December opens Queenstown's long southern-summer evenings beneath The Remarkables.
tradeoff: Closed for greens aerification 15–19 December 2026 and 14–19 December 2027. Confirm reopening and recovery conditions directly; holiday dates do not guarantee uninterrupted play.

why: December shares Singapore's coolest-month mean with January in Changi's long-term climate, giving the Serapong a small heat-relief benefit despite the wet season.
tradeoff: December is in the wettest part of the year; storm delays can outweigh the modest cooling. Private-club visitor rounds need advance confirmation.

why: December offers dry, cooler daytime golf away from Las Vegas's fierce summer heat; TPC Summerlin's private Bobby Weed layout winds through desert arroyos and canyons.
tradeoff: TPC Summerlin is a private membership club: establish eligible access before travel. Winter mornings are cold and frost can delay play.

why: December offers a quieter off-season links visit; Kennemer's sandy dune setting helps extend the playing season beyond summer when conditions permit.
tradeoff: Very short, cold and wet days; frost or winter greens may affect play. Confirm conditions and private-club visitor permission with the caddiemaster.
